newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia manufacturing pick-up modest - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia manufacturing pick-up modest - survey.

text.p: Australian manufacturers reported a very modest pre-Christmas pick-up but it nevertheless generated the first positive trends in production, sales and orders in 21 months, the Australian Chamber of Manufactures said on Monday.

"Moreover, the positive trends are expected to continue into the March quarter and pave the way for more significant growth later in 1997 as the benefits of the recent interest rate cuts begin to make themselves felt," the chamber said in its December quarter survey.

"Manufacturers remain comparatively positive about prospects for 1997 but the modest pace of the current growth points to the fragile nature of the trends," chamber chief executive Allan Handberg said in a statement.
The chamber surveyed 631 manufacturers with combined sales of more than A$25 billion and more than 92,000 employees.
It said 46 percent of those surveyed increased production in the December quarter and 24 percent reduced production.
Nine of the 12 manufacturing sectors achieved seasonal gains with strongest trends in food, beverages and tobacco, chemicals, petroleum and coal products and basic metals industries.
Investment also rose after easing in each of the eight previous quarters.
The chamber said 38 percent of manufacturers surveyed planned further production increases in the March quarter while 21 percent anticipated declines.
While the trends were generally positive they came from a low base, it said.
Average levels of capacity utilisation were at their highest point in 1996 but they were still significantly below those achieved in the past three Christmas periods, it said.
Manufacturing is operating at 73 percent of capacity, compared with 76 percent in the December quarter of 1993, 79 percent in 1994 and 76 percent in the 1995 December quarter.
The chamber said profit trends were also disappointing with companies reporting declines outnumbering those reporting gains in seven of the 12 sectors.
Companies reporting reductions in selling prices outnumbered those reporting gains for the sixth successive quarter, an indication of subdued consumer demand and tough competition.
Trends in exports and employment were also subdued, it said.
Although positive, export trends were comparatively weak compared with recent years, reflecting in part the appreciation of the Australian dollar.
This trend has now been apparent through most of 1996.
December quarter employment trends were mildly positive with 26 percent of respondents reporting increases and 23 percent reporting declines, the chamber said.
But the March quarter outlook points to further declines.
The findings were consistent with manufacturing growth of about 0.6 percent in the quarter and about 3.5 percent in 1996.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
